name: Sylphie Windwhisper
equipment: A leather-bound journal filled with storm giant rune translations
A shard of crystal that hums in thunderstorms
Robes of deep sky-blue with silver embroidery
A letter of introduction from the Vellum College (expired)
features: Unending Breath (Air Genasi racial — you can hold your breath indefinitely while you're not incapacitated)
Mingle with the Wind (Air Genasi racial — you can cast Levitate targeting yourself once per long rest, requiring no material components; CON is your spellcasting ability for this)
Font of Magic (5 sorcery points per long rest — can convert spell slots to sorcery points or vice versa: 1st=2pts, 2nd=3pts, 3rd=5pts; creating a slot costs points equal to level+1)

Metamagic: Twinned Spell (when you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, spend sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range; cantrips cost 1 point)
Metamagic: Quickened Spell (spend 2 sorcery points to change the casting time of a spell from 1 action to 1 bonus action)

Storm Sorcery: Tempestuous Magic (immediately before or after you cast a spell of 1st level or higher on your turn, you can use a bonus action to fly up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks)

Storm Sorcery: Heart of the Storm (at 6th level you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage — NOTE: this feature is gained at level 6, Sylphie is level 5 and does not yet have this feature; listed for reference)
Researcher (Sage feature — when you don't know a piece of lore, you often know where and from whom you can obtain it; the DM might rule that the knowledge you seek is in an almost inaccessible place)

personality.traits: I narrate my own thought process out loud, often in the third person — 'Sylphie notes the resonance frequency is wrong' — which my companions find either endearing or maddening depending on the hour. I gesticulate wildly when explaining magical theory, and small breezes follow my hands when I get excited. I collect unusual meteorological phenomena the way other people collect coins.
personality.ideals: Knowledge is not power — knowledge is responsibility. If I can understand the Vaunting, I can help fix it, and understanding requires rigorous study, not reckless heroism. Every mystery has a solution; the universe is not random, it is merely complex.
personality.bonds: My storm giant ancestor speaks to me in dreams — fragments, images, equations written in lightning. I believe the Vaunting is not merely an inherited hierarchy but a magical weave, and when it shattered, I felt it tear through my bloodline like a thunderclap. I owe it to my heritage to understand what happened and, if possible, to repair it.
personality.flaws: I prioritize understanding over urgency. When giants are attacking, my first instinct is to study the attack pattern rather than run. I also have a tendency to assume that every problem is an intellectual one, which means I sometimes miss the emotional reality of what people are going through.

appearance: Sylphie Windwhisper is immediately, unmistakably not entirely human. She is slight and willowy — five feet five inches tall and barely a hundred pounds — with the fragile, elongated build of someone designed more for flight than for walking. Her skin is a pale blue-white, the color of sky at the edge of the atmosphere, and it has a faint luminous quality in dim light, as though she were lit from within by distant lightning. Her hair is the most striking feature: a mass of silver-white strands that float and drift around her head as though she were perpetually underwater, or perpetually standing in an updraft. It never lies flat. In moments of strong emotion or spellcasting, her hair fans out in a corona around her skull, crackling with faint static discharge. Her eyes are solid pale grey with no visible iris — like looking into fog — and they brighten to white when she channels magic. Small things float near her when she is distracted: dust motes spiral upward, papers flutter, candle flames lean toward her as she passes. She wears layered robes of deep sky-blue over pale grey, the fabric embroidered with silver thread in patterns that look decorative but are actually storm giant rune-equations she has been trying to translate. A leather satchel hangs perpetually at her hip, stuffed with journals, loose papers, and a brass astrolabe that she consults far more often than necessary. Her hands are stained with ink — always, permanently, as though the stains have become part of her skin. A shard of crystal hangs from a cord around her neck, and it hums faintly whenever a storm is within fifty miles.
backstory:
Sylphie Windwhisper was not born during a storm, but her mother always said the wind changed direction the moment she drew her first breath. It was not a metaphor. The midwife reported that every window in the birthing room blew open simultaneously, and the candles did not just go out — they exploded upward in pillars of blue flame before sputtering back to normal. The midwife refused to return for any subsequent births.

Sylphie's air genasi heritage was obvious from infancy — the floating hair, the pale skin, the way small objects near her crib would drift upward as though gravity had forgotten them. Her parents, both human scholars at a small academy in Argentmere, were fascinated rather than frightened. They had her tested, prodded, examined by every mage willing to make the trip, and the conclusion was always the same: somewhere in Sylphie's bloodline, a storm giant had loved a mortal, and the elemental power of that union had been sleeping in the family tree for generations until it woke in her.

Sylphie grew up in libraries. She learned to read before she learned to control the breezes that followed her everywhere, and she found the former much easier than the latter. By twelve she was translating Primordial texts. By fifteen she had published a paper on the resonant frequencies of elemental magic that earned her a (politely declined) invitation to the Vellum College. By eighteen she had identified her life's work: the Vaunting.

The Vaunting fascinated Sylphie because it should not exist. Divine hierarchies were common enough among the gods — every pantheon had its pecking order — but the Vaunting was different. It was not merely a social structure imposed from above; it was a magical construct, woven into the fabric of giant-kind at a fundamental level. It shaped their behavior, their culture, their very biology. Storm giants grew largest because the Vaunting placed them highest. Hill giants were crude because the Vaunting placed them lowest. Remove the Vaunting, and what were giants? The question consumed her.

She got her answer the day the Vaunting shattered.

Sylphie was in her study at the academy, cross-referencing storm giant prophecy texts, when the psychic shockwave hit. She described it later as the sound of a harp with a thousand strings all snapping at once — not heard with the ears but felt in the blood, in the bones, in the part of her that was storm giant and elemental and ancient. She collapsed, unconscious for three days. When she woke, her hair had turned from dark brown to silver-white, and the crystal shard she wore around her neck — a gift from her mother, supposedly ordinary quartz — was humming.

The crystal has not stopped humming since. Sylphie believes it is resonating with the broken fragments of the Vaunting, like a tuning fork vibrating in sympathy with a shattered bell. She has spent the months since the breaking traveling the Cormorant Coast, collecting data — interviewing giant-kind, studying the sites where the Vaunting's influence was strongest, mapping the resonance patterns her crystal detects. Her theory is ambitious and possibly brilliant: the Vaunting is not destroyed, merely fragmented, and if the fragments can be located and understood, the weave can be rewoven.

Others call her naive. Giants are rampaging across the land, and she wants to study the phenomenon. But Sylphie has never been interested in fighting symptoms — she wants to cure the disease. And she is increasingly certain that the cure exists, written in storm giant prophecy, if she can only find the right text and translate it before the world tears itself apart.
